I'm 67 this year, been farming since I was 17 — that's 50 years on this same land in Quzhou. I've seen it all: the bad drought in '97, the flood in 2012, years when wheat hit 1.3 yuan per jin and years when it dropped below 0.9. My old man taught me, and I've taught my son, though he works at a factory in Handan now and only comes back for harvest. He sends about 2,000 yuan home each month, which helps a lot with buying inputs. My wife is 65 and still strong, so for field work it's mostly the two of us, with help when things get busy.

I have 10.1 mu of good flat land, all irrigated from the tube well. I keep 8 mu in wheat-maize double cropping — that's my foundation, never lets me down completely. The other 2.1 mu I plant chili. Chili is risky — prices jump around — but when it's good, it's better money than maize. My neighbor Lao Wang planted 3 mu of chili last year and did well, so I'm keeping my 2.1 mu in it. I don't dare more at my age; too much bending down for picking.

For wheat, I'll sow around October 12th. I use Jinmai 47, an improved variety I've grown for three years — reliable. I buy fresh seed this year, about 15 kg per mu, costs around 45 yuan. Before sowing, I spread base fertilizer: half a bag of compound fertilizer (50 kg bag for 2 mu, so 25 kg per mu) plus about 10 kg urea per mu. At jointing in late March, I topdress another 10 kg urea per mu. The extension station says 15 kg nitrogen per mu is enough, but I do a bit more — around 16 kg N per mu total — because my son's money lets me afford it, and I'd rather waste a little fertilizer than risk a big yield drop. The compound gives me some phosphorus and potassium too, about 4 kg each per mu.

I irrigate wheat three times: before winter freeze-up (most important), at jointing in March, and at heading in May if it doesn't rain. Pumping costs about 30 yuan per mu each time. It adds up, but without water there's no crop. I spray herbicide once in early spring and insecticide once if I see aphids.

For maize, there's no time to waste — we harvest wheat around June 15th and plant maize the same day or next. I use Zhengdan 958 hybrid, 2.5 kg per mu, about 60 yuan. At planting I put 20 kg compound fertilizer per mu in the row. Then at big trumpet stage in late July, I topdress about 15 kg urea per mu. Total N around 16 kg per mu. I irrigate twice — once at planting if it's dry, once at tasseling in early August. July usually brings some rain, so two times is enough most years. One pass of herbicide at planting, and I watch for armyworms in August.

For chili, I buy seedlings from the market in early May — about 2,000 plants per mu, cost around 80 yuan. I plow that 2.1 mu well in April and lay plastic mulch to keep moisture and control weeds. Base fertilizer is 30 kg compound per mu plus some chicken manure I bought. I topdress twice with urea during flowering and fruit set. Water three times — May, June, and July. Chili needs more pesticide: I spray for aphids and disease about 4 times. It's labor intensive — me and my wife spend many days there, and I hire 8 days of labor at 100 yuan per day for the peak harvest in August and September.

Total costs will run about 7,800 yuan. That's a lot, but with my son's help I can manage. I keep 2,000 yuan in reserve for emergencies — if the pump breaks or someone gets sick. At my age, I don't gamble. I do what works, watch my costs, and hope for a normal year. If wheat gives me 480 kg per mu and maize 520 kg per mu, and chili 300 kg per mu of dry pods, I'll be fine. Not rich, but fine.
